title: Critique: unlike a heavy coat, a nonphysical by-product follows from no physical law

statements.text: The heaviness of a polar bear's coat follows directly from the properties that make it warm. With dualistically conceived mental states it is the opposite: the physical laws that make brain states cause behavior do not explain why brain states give rise to conscious ones. The laws linking mind and brain are what Feigl called nomological danglers, brute additions to physical law, and there is no evident evolutionary explanation of such by-products.

sources.quote: Jackson’s point is true in general, but does not obviously apply to the case of mind.
Why there should have been by-products of that kind seems to have no obvious evolutionary explanation.
